newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends sharply down on China, hog worries.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends sharply down on China, hog worries.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed sharply lower against its U.S. counterpart on Monday on worries about possible new frictions with rival China and a crisis in the island's huge pork export industry, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.625 against Saturday's T$27.545 close.
Turnover through dealers was a frantic US$590.5 million.

The United Daily News quoted military intelligence as saying China planned an April joint-forces war games in coastal Fujian, Guangdong and Zhejiang provinces -- those nearest to Taiwan -- and said the exercises could amount to a protest over a visit to Taiwan by Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama.
Chinese provincial officials subsequently told Reuters they knew of no such exercise being planned.
Dealers said Taiwan's currency also was hit by the recent ban on pork exports following an outbreak of hog foot-and-mouth disease in Taiwan.
"If the export ban continues, Taiwan's overall exports, and therefore its economy, could take a big hit," said one dealer.
Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong told parliament on Monday that Taiwan's gross domestic product could lose up to half a percentage point in 1997 due to the pork crisis.
Dealers said they expected the local currency's downtrend to continue in the near term.
"I think the central bank seems to think the depreciation is acceptable, if not desired even," another dealer said.
A T$27.65-70 range was seen for Tuesday.
